before.title: Hecke Specht theory specialises to group Specht theory at q = 1
before.statement:
Let $F$ be a field, $q=1\in F$, and let $H_{F,1}(S_n)$ be the specialization of the generic type-A Hecke algebra at $v\mapsto1$, so that $H_{F,1}(S_n)\cong F[S_n]$ with $T_w\mapsto w$ ([[prop-group-algebra-and-finite-field-specializations-of-the-generic-hecke-algebra]]). Then the Hecke theory of this page specializes as follows.
1. The Murphy elements $m_\mu=\sum_{w\in S_\mu}T_w$ specialize to the row symmetrizers $\sum_{w\in S_\mu}w$, and the Murphy basis $\{m_{st}\}$ of $H_{F,1}(S_n)$ specializes to the Murphy basis of the group algebra $F[S_n]$ (the base change $\mathbb Z[S_n]\to F[S_n]$ of the integral Murphy basis).
2. For every $\lambda\vdash n$ the specialization of the page's Hecke Specht module $S^{\lambda}$ ([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]]) is the ordinary Specht module in the Dipper-James convention: $S^{\lambda}_{q=1}\cong S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ as $F[S_n]$-modules, with the standard polytabloid basis ([[thm-standard-polytabloid-basis]]); the specialized cell form is the standard bilinear form on $S^{\lambda}_k$ whose radical defines the James quotient $D^{\lambda}$ ([[def-modular-specht-form-and-radical-quotient]]).
3. The quantum characteristic of $q=1$ is $e=\operatorname{char}(F)$ when $\operatorname{char}(F)>0$, and $e=\infty$ when $\operatorname{char}(F)=0$ ([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]); in characteristic $p>0$ a partition is $e$-regular exactly when it is $p$-regular. Hence $D^{\lambda}_{q=1}\ne0$ exactly for $p$-regular $\lambda$ ([[thm-simple-type-a-hecke-modules-are-indexed-by-e-regular-partitions]]), and for non-$p$-regular $\lambda$ one has $\mathrm{rad}\,S^{\lambda}=S^{\lambda}$, so not every Specht module remains simple in characteristic $p$. This matches the group-side classification [[thm-modular-simple-modules-of-sn-are-the-p-regular-specht-heads]] and the conjugate-sign dictionary [[prop-p-regular-and-p-restricted-simple-labels-are-related-by-conjugate-sign-duality]]. In characteristic $0$ the specialization is split semisimple and all Specht modules are irreducible.
before.strategy: Base-change the Murphy cellular basis along $\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]\to F$, $v\mapsto1$: the structure constants are polynomials in $q$, so specialization gives a cellular basis of $F[S_n]$, and the cell modules specialize to the modules with the specialized triangular multiplication. The identification with the Dipper-James Specht module uses the printed p. 25 convention warning of the source together with the conjugate-sign duality of [[prop-p-regular-and-p-restricted-simple-labels-are-related-by-conjugate-sign-duality]]; the polytabloid/Murphy basis comparison is [[thm-standard-polytabloid-basis]]. The simple-label statement is the specialization of [[thm-simple-type-a-hecke-modules-are-indexed-by-e-regular-partitions]] at $e=\operatorname{char}(F)$, compared with [[thm-modular-simple-modules-of-sn-are-the-p-regular-specht-heads]]. The direction of information is one-way (this item imports the group classification and no group-side item depends on the Hecke theory). No choice is used.

before.title: The complete weight-one decomposition matrix for S3 at p=3
before.statement: Take $e=p=3$ and the weight-one configuration $n=3$, $\gamma=\varnothing$ of [[thm-weight-one-block-decomposition-pattern]]; the three partitions of $3$ with $3$-core $\varnothing$ are $\lambda_1=(3)\rhd\lambda_2=(2,1)\rhd\lambda_3=(1,1,1)$ ([[def-e-core-e-quotient-and-e-weight]]). The block of $S_3$ at $p=3$ therefore has the complete decomposition matrix, in the source's Weyl/simple normalisation and with rows and columns in the order $\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\lambda_3$, equal to $\begin{pmatrix}1&1&0\\0&1&1\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}$; applying the Schur functor and the conjugation/duality dictionary gives the Murphy Specht rows $[S^{\lambda_1}_{\mathrm M}]=[D^{\lambda_2}_{\mathrm M}]$, $[S^{\lambda_2}_{\mathrm M}]=[D^{\lambda_2}_{\mathrm M}]+[D^{\lambda_3}_{\mathrm M}]$, $[S^{\lambda_3}_{\mathrm M}]=[D^{\lambda_3}_{\mathrm M}]$, which in the page's $3$-regular labels $(3),(2,1)$ is the matrix $\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$ with rows $(3),(2,1),(1,1,1)$ ([[thm-nakayama-block-classification-for-symmetric-groups]], [[thm-modular-simple-modules-of-sn-are-the-p-regular-specht-heads]]); the group-side entries are verified directly from the two-dimensional model $S^{(2,1)}$ of characteristic $3$, whose all-ones vector spans a trivial submodule with sign quotient, together with $S^{(3)}=\operatorname{triv}$ and $S^{(1,1,1)}=\operatorname{sgn}$.
before.strategy: List the partitions of $3$ with $3$-core $\varnothing$: $(3)$ and $(1,1,1)$ remove their unique $3$-hook and $(2,1)$ has no $3$-hook, giving exactly the three labels in the stated dominance order. Apply the weight-one theorem to obtain the bidiagonal Weyl matrix, then the Schur functor and the conjugation/duality dictionary $S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm{DJ}}=(S^{\lambda'}_{\mathrm M})^{*}$, $D^{\lambda}_{\mathrm{DJ}}=(D^{\lambda'}_{\mathrm M})^{*}$ to pass from the Murphy rows to the group-side matrix with rows and columns in the $p$-regular labels $(3),(2,1)$, and finally compare with the direct computation from the standard module: in characteristic $3$ the all-ones vector of $S^{(2,1)}$ spans a trivial submodule with sign quotient, so the rows of $S^{(3)},S^{(2,1)},S^{(1,1,1)}$ are $(1,0),(1,1),(0,1)$ in the labels $(3),(2,1)$, and the simple labels are those of [[thm-modular-simple-modules-of-sn-are-the-p-regular-specht-heads]]. The two computations agree entry by entry, which is the verification of the example. No choice principle is used. Sources: Mathas, Proposition 5.38 and the accompanying discussion of $q=1$ (printed pp. 61-63); the published $S_3$ matrix.

direct_and_indirect_consumer_checks.actual_statement: Work over any commutative ring $R$ with $q\in R^{\times}$ and let $H=H_{R,q}(S_3)$ with generators $T_1,T_2$, the braid relation $T_1T_2T_1=T_2T_1T_2$ and quadratics $T_i^2=(q-1)T_i+q$. The Murphy cellular basis ([[thm-murphy-tableau-elements-form-a-cellular-basis]]) is indexed by the partitions $(3),(2,1),(1^3)$ ordered by dominance. Explicitly, with $*$ the antiautomorphism $T_w^*=T_{w^{-1}}$ ([[def-murphy-elements-and-murphy-tableau-elements]]): (a) for $\lambda=(3)$, $\mathrm{Std}(3)=\{s\}$ and $m_{ss}=m_{(3)}=1+T_1+T_2+T_1T_2+T_2T_1+T_1T_2T_1$; (b) for $\lambda=(2,1)$, $\mathrm{Std}(2,1)=\{t,u\}$ with $t=\begin{smallmatrix}1&2\\3\end{smallmatrix}$, $u=\begin{smallmatrix}1&3\\2\end{smallmatrix}$, and $m_{(2,1)}=1+T_1$ (the row symmetrizer of $S_{(2,1)}=\langle(1\,2)\rangle$), so that $m_{tt}=1+T_1$, $m_{tu}=(1+T_1)T_2$, $m_{ut}=T_2(1+T_1)$ and $m_{uu}=T_2(1+T_1)T_2$; (c) for $\lambda=(1^3)$, $\mathrm{Std}(1^3)=\{v\}$ and $m_{vv}=m_{(1^3)}=1$. In total $1+4+1=6=3!=|S_3|$ elements; the middle cell carries $|\mathrm{Std}(2,1)|^2=4$ basis elements, its two off-diagonal elements satisfy $m_{tu}^*=m_{ut}$, and the largest cell is spanned by $m_{ss}$, illustrating the cellular anti-involution. At $q=1$ this is the Murphy basis of the group algebra $\mathbb Z[S_3]$ ([[prop-hecke-specht-theory-specializes-to-group-specht-theory-at-q-one]]).

The products are then computed directly from $T_i^2=(q-1)T_i+q$ and the braid relation, and they match Mathas's Example 2.2(ii). No choice is used.

direct_and_indirect_consumer_checks.actual_statement: Let $F$ be a field, $q\in F^\times$, $\ell$ the quantum characteristic of $q$ ([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]) and $n\ge r$ as in the source. Let $S(n,r)$ be the type-A q-Schur algebra with the idempotent $e$ of the weight $(1^r)$, so that $eS(n,r)e\cong H(r)$, and let $f_{n,r}:S(n,r)\text{-mod}\to H(r)\text{-mod}$, $V\mapsto eV$, be the exact Schur functor with left adjoint $h_{n,r}$ ([[def-schur-idempotent-and-schur-functor-for-type-a-q-schur-algebras]]). Let $L_n(\lambda)$ be the irreducible $S(n,r)$-module for an $\ell$-restricted $\lambda\vdash r$, and $L_n(\lambda)^1$ its first level. Then (i) $f_{n-1,r-1}\bigl(L_n(\lambda)^1\bigr)=f_{n,r}\bigl(L_n(\lambda)\bigr)\bigl\downarrow_{H(r-1)}$ as $H(r-1)$-modules, naturally; (ii) for $S(n,r)$-modules $W,V$ with $W^{(e)}=W$ and $V_{(e)}=0$ one has $\operatorname{Hom}_{S(n,r)}(W,V)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{H(r)}(fW,fV)$, so the functor detects and preserves the relevant Hom spaces and (being exact) transfers composition multiplicities of first-level modules; (iii) if $\lambda$ is $\ell$-restricted then the socle of $L_n(\lambda)^1$ restricted to the Levi subalgebra $U(n-1)$ consists of $\ell$-restricted labels; at $q=1$ (so $\ell=p$ in characteristic $p$; characteristic zero gives $\ell=\infty$) the specialization $H(r)\to kS_r$ of ([[prop-hecke-specht-theory-specializes-to-group-specht-theory-at-q-one]]) makes (i)-(iii) statements about $kS_r$-modules and the simple $kS_{r-1}$-modules of ([[thm-schur-functor-sends-weyl-and-simple-modules-to-specht-and-hecke-simple-modules]]).
direct_and_indirect_consumer_checks.actual_strategy: Complete argument, Brundan 1998 §5.5-5.7 (complete 34-page author manuscript, pp. 30-32) and Kleshchev I §2.12(v), whose citation is replaced by this proof-bearing comparison. (i) Take the permitted stable rank $n=r$ and write the $(1^r)$-weight idempotent of $S(n,r)$; by §3.22 of the source the weight belongs to the level-1 summand, and deleting the last (level) coordinate of the weight identifies it with the $(1^{r-1})$-weight of $S(n-1,r-1)$, while the generators $T_1,\dots,T_{r-2}$ act identically before and after the deletion. Hence both sides are equal as explicit simultaneous weight spaces, naturally in $V$; this uses neither semisimplicity nor an identification of cellular and crystal labels. (ii) Is Brundan's Lemma 5.6(i)-(ii), proved by the adjunction $h\dashv f$ and the submodule $V_{(e)}$; (iii) is Lemma 5.7, whose proof uses the good-node description of the socle and shows that $i\in R^{good}(\lambda)$ implies $\lambda(i)$ is $\ell$-restricted. Composition multiplicities: apply the exact functor $f$ to a composition series of the first-level module; a surviving restricted simple maps to a Hecke simple, a killed simple contributes nothing, and by (ii) the multiplicity of a selected surviving simple is preserved. The $q=1$ specialization is the Hecke/group identification of the batch-20 item. This is the exact replacement for Kleshchev I §2.12(v) as recorded by the SYMR-9 evidence report; Step 3 must keep the weight-idempotent computation explicit.

direct_and_indirect_consumer_checks.actual_statement: Let $k$ be a splitting field of characteristic $p>0$ (equivalently the residue field of the fixed splitting $p$-modular system, [[def-splitting-p-modular-system-for-a-finite-group]], [[def-p-blocks-by-primitive-central-idempotents]]) and let $n\ge0$. Two Specht modules $S^{\lambda}_k,S^{\mu}_k$ of $k[S_n]$ lie in the same block of $k[S_n]$ if and only if $\lambda,\mu\vdash n$ have the same $p$-core ([[def-e-core-e-quotient-and-e-weight]]). Consequently the blocks of $k[S_n]$ are indexed by the pairs $(\gamma,w)$ with $\gamma$ a $p$-core, $w\in\mathbb N_0$ and $n=|\gamma|+pw$, and the block of $S^{\lambda}_k$ is $(c_p(\lambda),w_p(\lambda))$ with $w_p(\lambda)=(n-|c_p(\lambda)|)/p$ ([[prop-core-quotient-size-and-weight-formula]]).
direct_and_indirect_consumer_checks.actual_strategy: Specialise the Hecke block theorem at $q=1$. By [[prop-hecke-specht-theory-specializes-to-group-specht-theory-at-q-one]] the specialisation $H_{k,1}(S_n)\cong k[S_n]$ carries the Hecke Specht modules of this page to the group Specht modules of $k[S_n]$ in the Dipper-James convention and has quantum characteristic $e=\operatorname{char}(k)=p$, so [[cor-type-a-hecke-specht-modules-are-in-the-same-block-iff-their-labels-have-the-same-e-core]] gives: $S^{\lambda}_k$ and $S^{\mu}_k$ lie in the same block of $k[S_n]$ if and only if $\lambda$ and $\mu$ have the same $p$-core. The parametrisation by pairs $(\gamma,w)$ is then the size formula of [[prop-core-quotient-size-and-weight-formula]] at $e=p$ together with the block decomposition by primitive central idempotents in [[def-p-blocks-by-primitive-central-idempotents]]. This is Mathas, Corollary 5.37 specialised at $q=1$ (printed pp. 61-63 with Chapters 1 and 3-5); O'Donovan, Theorem 1 (arXiv:1708.04365, p. 1) states the same classification by the independent Young-module and Brauer-quotient route and is recorded here as an independent confirmation of the statement, not as the proof route of this page. No choice principle is used.
direct_and_indirect_consumer_checks.assessment: Consumes retained all-field ordinary q1 module identification and e=p together with signed same-core block theorem; NEW50 actual proof supplies these. No removed simplicity claim.

direct_and_indirect_consumer_checks.actual_statement: Local removable-hook counts do not determine the block. Take $p=3$ and the partitions $\lambda=(5)$ and $\mu=(4,1)$ of $5$. The hook lengths of $(5)$ are $5,4,3,2,1$, so exactly one removable $3$-hook exists, namely at $(1,3)$; the hook lengths of $(4,1)$ are $5,3,2,1,1$, so exactly one removable $3$-hook exists, at $(1,2)$. Thus both partitions have the same number (one) of removable $3$-hooks, but their $3$-cores differ: $C_3((5))=(2)$ while $C_3((4,1))=(1,1)$ ([[def-e-core-e-quotient-and-e-weight]], [[thm-e-core-is-independent-of-the-rim-hook-removal-order]]). Since Specht modules lie in the same block if and only if their labels have the same $p$-core ([[thm-nakayama-block-classification-for-symmetric-groups]]), no local count of removable hooks can replace the top-packed abacus test.
direct_and_indirect_consumer_checks.actual_strategy: Compute the hook lengths of both partitions directly from the diagrams, list the hooks of length $3$ and check which of them are removable (their removal leaves a partition), obtaining one removable $3$-hook for each. Compute the top-packed $3$-abaci: for $(5)$ the $\beta$-set is $\{5\}$ with core bead $\{2\}$ and $C_3((5))=(2)$; for $(4,1)$ the $\beta$-set is $\{5,1\}$ with top-packed configuration $\{2,1\}$ and $C_3((4,1))=(1,1)$. The two cores are distinct $3$-cores (both of size $2$), so by the Nakayama classification the two labels cannot lie in the same block ([[thm-nakayama-block-classification-for-symmetric-groups]]). The counterexample is verified by these two independent computations; no choice principle is used, and it is derived from the abacus method of the registered Tomczak lecture notes (§4.1).

direct_and_indirect_consumer_checks.actual_statement: Let $k$ be a splitting field of characteristic $p>0$ and $\lambda\vdash n$ a partition of $p$-weight $w_p(\lambda)=0$, that is, a $p$-core. Then the block $B$ of $k[S_n]$ containing $S^{\lambda}_k$ ([[thm-nakayama-block-classification-for-symmetric-groups]]) contains exactly one Specht label, namely $\lambda$; its decomposition matrix is the $1\times1$ matrix $(1)$, so $D^{\lambda}$ is both the unique simple and the unique projective indecomposable of $B$; its Cartan matrix is $(1)$; the block algebra is a full matrix algebra over $k$; and $B$ has trivial defect group, that is, defect zero in the fixed splitting modular system ([[def-defect-group-and-numerical-defect-of-a-block]]).
direct_and_indirect_consumer_checks.actual_strategy: Nakayama's classification and $w_p(\lambda)=0$ leave no other partition of $n$ in the block: any $\mu\ne\lambda$ in it would satisfy $|\mu|=|\lambda|+pw_p(\mu)>n$. A $p$-core is $p$-regular ([[def-e-core-e-quotient-and-e-weight]]), so $D^{\lambda}\ne0$ and the decomposition matrix of the block is the single entry $d_{\lambda\lambda}$; dominance unitriangularity ([[thm-symmetric-group-decomposition-matrix-is-dominance-unitriangular]]) gives $d_{\lambda\lambda}=1$, and $C=D^{\top}D=(1)$ by [[thm-cartan-matrix-is-d-transpose-d]]. Hence the projective cover $P(\lambda)$ has $D^{\lambda}$ as its only composition factor, with multiplicity one; comparing dimensions gives $P(\lambda)=D^{\lambda}$, so $B$ has a projective simple module. [[thm-defect-zero-blocks-are-simple-algebras]] then yields the full-matrix description, the uniqueness of the simple, and the trivial defect group; the block notion is that of [[def-p-blocks-by-primitive-central-idempotents]]. No choice principle is used.

authentic_before.title: Hecke Specht theory specialises to group Specht theory at q = 1
authentic_before.statement:
Let $F$ be a field, $q=1\in F$, and let $H_{F,1}(S_n)$ be the specialization of the generic type-A Hecke algebra at $v\mapsto1$, so that $H_{F,1}(S_n)\cong F[S_n]$ with $T_w\mapsto w$ ([[prop-group-algebra-and-finite-field-specializations-of-the-generic-hecke-algebra]]). Then the Hecke theory of this page specializes as follows.
1. The Murphy elements $m_\mu=\sum_{w\in S_\mu}T_w$ specialize to the row symmetrizers $\sum_{w\in S_\mu}w$, and the Murphy basis $\{m_{st}\}$ of $H_{F,1}(S_n)$ specializes to the Murphy basis of the group algebra $F[S_n]$ (the base change $\mathbb Z[S_n]\to F[S_n]$ of the integral Murphy basis).
2. For every $\lambda\vdash n$ the specialization of the page's Hecke Specht module $S^{\lambda}$ ([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]]) is the ordinary Specht module in the Dipper-James convention: $S^{\lambda}_{q=1}\cong S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ as $F[S_n]$-modules, with the standard polytabloid basis ([[thm-standard-polytabloid-basis]]); the specialized cell form is the standard bilinear form on $S^{\lambda}_k$ whose radical defines the James quotient $D^{\lambda}$ ([[def-modular-specht-form-and-radical-quotient]]).
3. The quantum characteristic of $q=1$ is $e=\operatorname{char}(F)$ when $\operatorname{char}(F)>0$, and $e=\infty$ when $\operatorname{char}(F)=0$ ([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]); in characteristic $p>0$ a partition is $e$-regular exactly when it is $p$-regular. Hence $D^{\lambda}_{q=1}\ne0$ exactly for $p$-regular $\lambda$ ([[thm-simple-type-a-hecke-modules-are-indexed-by-e-regular-partitions]]), and for non-$p$-regular $\lambda$ one has $\mathrm{rad}\,S^{\lambda}=S^{\lambda}$, so not every Specht module remains simple in characteristic $p$. This matches the group-side classification [[thm-modular-simple-modules-of-sn-are-the-p-regular-specht-heads]] and the conjugate-sign dictionary [[prop-p-regular-and-p-restricted-simple-labels-are-related-by-conjugate-sign-duality]]. In characteristic $0$ the specialization is split semisimple and all Specht modules are irreducible.
authentic_before.strategy: Base-change the Murphy cellular basis along $\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]\to F$, $v\mapsto1$: the structure constants are polynomials in $q$, so specialization gives a cellular basis of $F[S_n]$, and the cell modules specialize to the modules with the specialized triangular multiplication. The identification with the Dipper-James Specht module uses the printed p. 25 convention warning of the source together with the conjugate-sign duality of [[prop-p-regular-and-p-restricted-simple-labels-are-related-by-conjugate-sign-duality]]; the polytabloid/Murphy basis comparison is [[thm-standard-polytabloid-basis]]. The simple-label statement is the specialization of [[thm-simple-type-a-hecke-modules-are-indexed-by-e-regular-partitions]] at $e=\operatorname{char}(F)$, compared with [[thm-modular-simple-modules-of-sn-are-the-p-regular-specht-heads]]. The direction of information is one-way (this item imports the group classification and no group-side item depends on the Hecke theory). No choice is used.

authentic_before.title: The complete weight-one decomposition matrix for S3 at p=3
authentic_before.statement: Take $e=p=3$ and the weight-one configuration $n=3$, $\gamma=\varnothing$ of [[thm-weight-one-block-decomposition-pattern]]; the three partitions of $3$ with $3$-core $\varnothing$ are $\lambda_1=(3)\rhd\lambda_2=(2,1)\rhd\lambda_3=(1,1,1)$ ([[def-e-core-e-quotient-and-e-weight]]). The block of $S_3$ at $p=3$ therefore has the complete decomposition matrix, in the source's Weyl/simple normalisation and with rows and columns in the order $\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\lambda_3$, equal to $\begin{pmatrix}1&1&0\\0&1&1\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}$; applying the Schur functor and the conjugation/duality dictionary gives the Murphy Specht rows $[S^{\lambda_1}_{\mathrm M}]=[D^{\lambda_2}_{\mathrm M}]$, $[S^{\lambda_2}_{\mathrm M}]=[D^{\lambda_2}_{\mathrm M}]+[D^{\lambda_3}_{\mathrm M}]$, $[S^{\lambda_3}_{\mathrm M}]=[D^{\lambda_3}_{\mathrm M}]$, which in the page's $3$-regular labels $(3),(2,1)$ is the matrix $\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$ with rows $(3),(2,1),(1,1,1)$ ([[thm-nakayama-block-classification-for-symmetric-groups]], [[thm-modular-simple-modules-of-sn-are-the-p-regular-specht-heads]]); the group-side entries are verified directly from the two-dimensional model $S^{(2,1)}$ of characteristic $3$, whose all-ones vector spans a trivial submodule with sign quotient, together with $S^{(3)}=\operatorname{triv}$ and $S^{(1,1,1)}=\operatorname{sgn}$.
authentic_before.strategy: List the partitions of $3$ with $3$-core $\varnothing$: $(3)$ and $(1,1,1)$ remove their unique $3$-hook and $(2,1)$ has no $3$-hook, giving exactly the three labels in the stated dominance order. Apply the weight-one theorem to obtain the bidiagonal Weyl matrix, then the Schur functor and the conjugation/duality dictionary $S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm{DJ}}=(S^{\lambda'}_{\mathrm M})^{*}$, $D^{\lambda}_{\mathrm{DJ}}=(D^{\lambda'}_{\mathrm M})^{*}$ to pass from the Murphy rows to the group-side matrix with rows and columns in the $p$-regular labels $(3),(2,1)$, and finally compare with the direct computation from the standard module: in characteristic $3$ the all-ones vector of $S^{(2,1)}$ spans a trivial submodule with sign quotient, so the rows of $S^{(3)},S^{(2,1)},S^{(1,1,1)}$ are $(1,0),(1,1),(0,1)$ in the labels $(3),(2,1)$, and the simple labels are those of [[thm-modular-simple-modules-of-sn-are-the-p-regular-specht-heads]]. The two computations agree entry by entry, which is the verification of the example. No choice principle is used. Sources: Mathas, Proposition 5.38 and the accompanying discussion of $q=1$ (printed pp. 61-63); the published $S_3$ matrix.
